claims.text: The initial as-cast or homogenized high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Demanding mechanical loading triggers local compositional fluctuations in the alloy.
Loading-induced compositional fluctuations promote nucleation of nanoscale brittle precipitates.
The nanoscale precipitates form preferentially along grain boundaries.
Applied mechanical load induces local segregation or stress-assisted phase decomposition.
Stress-assisted segregation or phase decomposition causes brittle precipitates to nucleate and grow along grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary precipitates act as stress concentrators.
The precipitate-associated microstructural changes reduce crack blunting and plastic energy absorption.
Reduced crack blunting and plastic deformation lower fracture toughness and lead to brittle fracture under further loading.
Loaded samples will contain more detectable nanoscale precipitates than the initial or unloaded baseline.
Loaded samples will exhibit lower fracture toughness than the baseline.
Loading will cause a transition from ductile to brittle fracture behavior relative to the baseline.
High applied stress and high strain rate, with elevated temperature where applicable, can exceed a threshold for stress-induced precipitation.
Below the stress-induced precipitation threshold, the alloy will maintain its toughness.
The stress and temperature threshold and transformation kinetics depend on alloy composition and microstructure.
